**[Watch My Testimony Opposing House Bill 2548](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fleg-my.sharepoint.com%2Fpersonal%2Fbreesev_oregonlegislature_gov%2F_layouts%2F15%2Fstream.aspx%3Fid=%252Fpersonal%252Fbreesev%255Foregonlegislature%255Fgov%252FDocuments%252F2025%2520Session%252FVideo%2520Clips%252F2025%252E03%252E12%2520Rep%2520Breese%252DIverson%2520Testimony%2520HB%25202548%252Emp4%26referrer=StreamWebApp%252EWeb%26referrerScenario=AddressBarCopied%252Eview%252E6ceb6a24%252D085c%252D4792%252Daf7b%252D4b5e84099890/1/0101019595898108-aa5e79a8-a05d-4f22-b5f5-b7ec30e61265-000000/zKPGARkeo4hcLMxmb3Ep2BU2mndMkCh-ck9UKBgI1C8=396)**
Chair Grayber, Vice Chairs Elmer and Munoz, members of the committee,
For the record, my name is Vikki Breese Iverson from Prineville and I represent House District 59. I am here in opposition to HB 2548.
This bill, while perhaps well-intentioned, places undue burdens on rural Oregonians—like the good people I represent in Crook, Jefferson, and Deschutes Counties.
Farm life is continually under threat by rule making - and not just from one agencies but rather from multiple agencies and with regard to multiple issue sets. You shouldn’t need a degree in public policy, a compliance team, and multiple lawyers to run a farm.
Oregon farmers already face unpredictable business challenges, such as weather, product prices, inflation - HB 2548 sets up another inflexible government hurdle to this industry.
We need to emphasize the Oregon way of working together, for practical solutions, over handing down more mandates.
HB 2548 is not designed to be nimble to market conditions, Mother Nature or the nature of a family run business. Many of the businesses which will be impacted don’t work in a cookie cutter, regulatory mentality.
I am personally concerned it will raise costs of goods, stifle local jobs, and erode the independence we value in Oregon. I have said it before and will say it again - we don’t need more red tape from Salem. We need policies which will allow more local control for our diverse landscapes, ag sectors and communities.
I strongly urge this committee to oppose HB 2548 and protect rural Oregon’s voice.

#
**It seems I live rent-free in the minds of some of my Republican colleagues.**
I wish they’d spend even _a fraction_ of that time thinking about lowering costs for hardworking families instead of obsessing over culture war issues.
But here’s the truth: MAGA Republicans aren’t just coming after me. They’re coming after everything we’re fighting for.
And they’ll do anything to distract from the fact that they’re dismantling our government and advancing a Billionaire First MAGA agenda that would leave families, veterans, homeowners, and renters in Delaware and across the country behind. _This isn’t leadership._
**The best way we can respond is to send a powerful message that we WON’T be distracted.** We have the opportunity to do just that by posting a big fundraising report at the end of the month.
**I want the GOP to see exactly how many people have my back and that their efforts to tear us down won’t diminish our fight to try and make this world a better place for all of us.**

The government is set to run out of money tonight at midnight. Once again, Republicans have brought us to the brink of a government shutdown. Let’s talk about how we got here. Over in Congress right now, we’re debating a procedural budget bill to keep the government funded. The spending plan that Republicans put forward that we’re debating includes funding cuts for hospitals, schools, child care centers, and veterans. But that’s not all. This bill will also essentially give Donald Trump a blank check too — one that removes the guardrails from Congress on how he should spend taxpayer funds. So perhaps Trump and Musk want to shovel $75 million of ALS treatment funding over to anti-vaccine research instead. This Republican bill says that’s okay. And say Trump and Musk decide to fire another 25,000 veterans or kick one million old people out of nursing homes. This Republican bill says that’s okay. Republicans are refusing to sit at the negotiating table with Democrats to work on a spending plan in good faith. They are saying they’ll vote to keep the government open **only if** we cut money for these critical programs and give Donald Trump more unchecked power. So I'm voting NO on the Republican shutdown bill. NO on handing Donald Trump and Elon Musk a blank check to spend your taxpayer money however they want. NO on cutting funding that helps families put food on the table and crack down on wealthy tax cheats. Make no mistake: Republicans are forging ahead with their plan to shut down the government. They don’t care about the consequences it will have on you or your family. That is why I am here in the Senate standing up and fighting back. I’m going to do everything in my power to keep our government up and running for American families — not just for Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and a handful of billionaires. Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth

**SOUTH CAROLINA** The SC House debated the state budget this week. The Columbia Swamp proposed the largest budget in state history, growing spending by over 10% from last year. But the **South Carolina Freedom Caucus** , building off of President Trump's mandate to slash spending, offered a conservative alternative budget that cut $1 billion in spending and would use that money to lower income tax rates from 6.2% down to 5%, making it the largest tax cut in history. Led by SCFC Chairman Jordan Pace, they offered 120 amendments (!!) to get rid of non-essential services and waste in the budget. **Unfortunately, the "Republican" supermajority defeated each and every one of them.** Here are some of the amendments they offered:
---
* Defund a climate change program ([defeated 85-22](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjozlsBOUyvRoQkvOsisTSzyBSeu8J82FUEKgaku1kzrbFfIceWRaDufB4rE2G0JXXA-3D-3DQ4ls_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerLddZHQJhGCwmIaBLLhcdoq-2FBA5vh9wxOL1arGFjgzQ0PiW3aZlSpsx9SItHJ2XiZ-2F5Y-2FhvDlMjhyqe2E2FcTQwLE9lXoBoMNB1SCLtkTGdzmIaCzYp7KbDaufM76eGwLEStaECvOP8NN6lulMScRW6FrRRFalDm11NOBvWDKHbVxsnJDXItAo0kiUw6BPbEZe-2FPQ-2F8VVzwzuMTw4aYYwXrUNYWCpysiu2RU-2BQFLHa0Y-3D))
* Defund "woke" training in government agencies ([defeated 87-19](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjozlsBOUyvRoQkvOsisTSzyBSeu8J82FUEKgaku1kzrboIZN76VLel-2BVLNjoDgaJjA-3D-3D85Iz_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerLddZHQJhGCwmIaBLLhcdoq-2FBA5vh9wxOL1arGFjgzQ0PiW3aZlSpsx9SItHJ2XiZ-2F5Y-2FhvDlMjhyqe2E2FcTQ-2BtHrvBMVx2qCASwmzOq9-2FiNYrlK1MtyIpms0FLK3-2FY4cWZc-2BQ3TaJHjsjsNB6fZMdbi7WXIvRMRrvH1ZSJLAb1L-2FOWKTffC6uijNezr3KVQ-2Fcc-2BTJ2oOvyUDLxNKnLuHF21SQ8UudYWx-2F8P5PtptBo-3D))
* Defund Hollywood subsidies, sports marketing, and subsidies for electric vehicle charging stations ([defeated 92-16](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjozlsBOUyvRoQkvOsisTSzyBSeu8J82FUEKgaku1kzrb-2F46ZLyz4KlUP37vvmtr2Mw-3D-3DxBho_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerLddZHQJhGCwmIaBLLhcdoq-2FBA5vh9wxOL1arGFjgzQ0PiW3aZlSpsx9SItHJ2XiZ-2F5Y-2FhvDlMjhyqe2E2FcTQ5OVEY7l2s9QuFBPMqpMJAQzVt6pkareu3zfhDAIK0imYE-2BB6p-2FUTP8YFwefPOf-2FSVYzGIxyFe5yHq5tZIhLwOKL-2Fuwtb-2FHwmuSIv5HAPK7N6LIMihg6k2BCToiE8GDzjAaxO4qwCBVhrgmQkqteZYA-3D))

---
**Let's be crystal clear - so-called "Republicans" in South Carolina are actively supporting The Left's top priorities.** In previous years, they got away with this because there was no freedom caucus calling them out on it. But thanks to the SC Freedom Caucus, these RINOs are being constantly exposed. Here's a video of SCFC Chairman Pace offering an amendment to cut $500,000 for ONE position within the state library. Note how the Uniparty's Rep. Gil Gatch belittles Pace for "having no idea" how this affects the rest of the budget (as if that's relevant):

[](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjnQLx7G1JfeswbLt4EUKsYMRT4u9yOsOU3aZQobiOxJ0CeT8wvx1zUJ6KENn62eRyQ-3D-3D9c6S_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerLddZHQJhGCwmIaBLLhcdoq-2FBA5vh9wxOL1arGFjgzQ0PiW3aZlSpsx9SItHJ2XiZ-2F5Y-2FhvDlMjhyqe2E2FcTQ46G6Vd0icRi68ACfNHk6mngJ-2FCkFNgpCxaMBRFzUtRVpi2Yv3mAPmAtLWE4pLq6bII8h8hdmZ5ikB99oXlol0BUm-2FgDnx1iF4jCK1x79bPOxZi434thfDXOhX3df0hI5XjRWns7RX7vTWHPnMQT1FM-3D)

clean_body: This race is going to be close, and our rights and freedoms depend on it. | = Team, I’m no stranger to how close statewide races in Wisconsin can be. Last fall, my race was the most expensive Senate race our state has ever seen — and it all came down to just a few votes. This year, the stakes are just as high. And now, Elon Musk has weighed in—making it clear that the far right is all-in on flipping control of the court. We can't let them win. We don't have a "Please and Thank You" foreign policy in this country. Trump wants to bring production back to the U.S. and a "Please and Thank You" foreign policy will not be enough to incentivize companies and nations to produce here or to treat American products fairly abroad.
The *only* alternative to tariffs is to continue doing what we've been doing for the past 30 years. Newsflash: It's not working. No one wants higher prices. I don't believe it will come to that. But Trump has a plan. It appears reasonable to me and we will find out sooner than later if his bet was worth it. I'm rooting that it is and that we can make America great again.

name: Marcy Kaptur
subject: Putin is not our friend.
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP33/1/95655/images/kaptur-email-header-2.png]

Friend,

The America I know doesn't turn its back on our allies. We stand for liberty wherever it is threatened, and we don't side with murderous tyrants over democratic freedom fighters.

When President Trump attempted to humiliate Ukrainian President Zelenskyy in the Oval Office, he didn't just betray our ally. He betrayed our nation's values.

Let's be clear, friend: Vladimir Putin is not our friend. He's a ruthless dictator who has ordered numerous journalists, activists, and political opponents murdered. His war in Ukraine is a flagrant, illegal attempt to seize more land and power.

As the co-chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus, I won't stand by while our 5-time draft-dodging president abandons our allies and bows down to Moscow. I'll always fight for liberty and democracy, at home and abroad.

I'm grateful to have you with me in that fight, friend.

With you,

— Marcy

My parents taught me a very important lesson when I was younger: **We have a responsibility to ensure that everyone gets a fair shot in life.**
I’ve carried that lesson with me every step of my life — from my time as a voting rights lawyer, to leading Wayne State Law School, to serving as Secretary of State.
[**Now, I’m running for Governor of Michigan to continue that work. ### _**Oh ...Canada??**_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e0b74a98-a178-413b-9b41-0020d7c30e36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Look, we've seen a lot of insane headlines in the Trump era, but the fact an actual U.S. congressman felt the need to introduce a bill preventing America from **invading Canada**? _That 's a new level of dystopian absurdity._ Yet, here we are.
Rep. Shri Thanedar, Detroit Democrat, has co-sponsored a bill saying, "_no, let 's not go to war with Canada_." Why? Because we have a frothing, fatuous, clementine-faced madman as president who keeps questioning Canada's autonomy with expansionist rhetoric about its becoming "our beautiful 51st state."
It becomes no less less absurd, but a lot less funny, when members of our intelligence community leak that if our "President" spoke this way about a non-ally _they 'd expect an invasion._ It loses more non-existent luster when you realize **a French-nuclear-attack submarine has docked in Novia Scotia, 300 miles from the U.S. border.** So, whatever, (as Wolverine called Deadpool) "God's Perfect Idiot" is doing, our allies aren't taking chances. And the thing about placing nuclear subs in play is _mistakes happen_. So, thanks again, business Republicans. "not voting for the guy but party." Good job.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4ebb0654-c814-4bc5-8215-b19640af93d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Also, I know the French and Canadians have said this isn't related to Trump, that a plan was already in the works. But, tell me if they'd say anything else if its purpose were very different. _Let 's be clear:_ Trump's worldview is driven by resentment and delusions of power. Canada--with a functioning democracy, progressive policies and refusal to bow to him--is like a giant middle finger to the black hole parading around in a meatsuit putting his grubby, toddler-esque fingers on everything he can stroke.

So yeah, I'd bet he'd love to start barking about Trudeau being a "globalist tyrant" before slapping his name on the CN Tower. And with a cadre of far-right freaks whispering in his ear (the shot one showing no real sign of injury), who see democracy as nuisance, not principle, _**who knows some lunatic "preemptive strike" plan won't emerge from the Mar-a-Lago crapper--aka the stolen, classified-document storage unit?**_
Canada is literally **worried** that the U.S. might, under Trump, become unstable enough to lash out militarily. This isn't _The Handmaid 's Tale_ creeping into reality--it's history repeating itself. Right-wing mooks always search for external enemies, and when Trump runs outta targets at home, why wouldn't he look for a neighbor to bully? His MAGA hordes already believe Canadian to be some kinda Maoist villain-state, so a propaganda campaign practically writes itself.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c97bc169-279c-4a88-bee1-8b56cdfdbfe9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The good news? Canada, besides having a prime minister who can string sentences together, has an actual _functioning_ democracy--one that protects itself from aspiring despots. But the bill Thanedar co-sponsored? A grim reminder we must speak openly --indeed raise our voices in America and around the world--in pre-protest. Because if we let Trump have free rein, we won't just be fighting for the soul of America--we may have a South Park movie come to life--a horrific one not the slightest bit funny.
* * *
### _**... Other stories we're watching**_
* Democrats have done a valiant job fighting a GOP continuing resolution that NEEDS Senate Democrats to overcome a filibuster. We were in great shape to block it & shut down the government--something I'd never normally push--but the Republican bill endorses the Trump/DOGE slush fund lacking any oversight.
House Dem Rosa DeLauro (CT-03): "..it gives Elon Musk and President Donald Trump even more flexibility to steal from the middle class, from seniors, from veterans, from working people, from small businesses and from farmers, all to pay for tax breaks for billionaires." Everyone from AOC to Rep. Nancy Pelosi, Senators Mark Warner to Chris Van Hollen--all wings of the party--have stood firm against it. But last night, in an inexplicable move**Praised By Donald Trump** , Senate Leader Chuck Schumer said he'd give Republicans the votes.

* Today [veterans are marching in Washington, DC,](https://substack.com/redirect/2b6ca720-1fb3-4736-b41b-830697fa9318?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to protest Donald Trump and support everything from freedom in Ukraine to Social Security. They picked today because it's 3/14--or the 14th Amendment Section III--which says those who engage in "insurrection" must be barred from office. Trump never should've been able to run again. He only could due to the failure of Mitch McConnell, our hijacked Supreme Court and a GOP Congress' refusal to hold him accountable.

As we speed toward spring, I thought it would be good to give you a rundown of long session in Salem. I will keep these comments to the pillars we discussed for our communities to be successful in Senate District 5- Housing, childcare, health care, and education. **Housing** As I hope you are aware, I have been the Vice Chair of Housing and Development Committee trying to tackle our housing crisis for the past 5 years now. Over this time, the Legislature has passed many bills, discussed numerous ideas and spent over $2.6 billion dollars in housing. I say this, because the problem has not been solved. Building permits are lower now than they were when the Governor declared an emergency over two years ago. I often wonder how that can be. I don’t have the specific answer in my pocket, but I do know the answers lie in three things: land, regulations and infrastructure. These three areas are vital to solving the housing crisis in Oregon, I would even dare to say, nothing else matters but these three areas to help with housing. Land has become a political hot potato in Salem and the Legislature invested hundreds of millions so far in infrastructure. We now land on regulations. I have two bills that will streamline the land use approval process inside the UGB of cities (974) and then a “shot clock” bill (6) that will require building permits are approved or denied in 45 days or less. These two bills can speed up the home building process dramatically. We are having hearings and lots of discussion on these two bills in the Legislature. **Childcare** Childcare has been a huge part of my passion in Salem. We must have more affordable options and childcare facilities so our work force can work. Young parents are the backbone of a growing community, we need them badly up and down the coast and rural Oregon. I have a bill to site childcare in affordable housing projects (439) that has been stalled in committee because of union bosses not wanting to give in on prevailing wage requirements. Mind you, we have an agreement to not do prevailing wage on affordable housing projects now, but if you add just one childcare facility there the whole project must go to prevailing wage. This can increase costs for the project by 50% or more and ultimately moves the project to unattainable. It is disappointing to see unions blocking this legislation to carve out childcare facilities to site on affordable housing projects. I hope they reconsider. We will have further reports on education and health care as bills in those committees heat up and move to the floor. I am watching those committees every week to make sure we are continuing to invest in our children, seniors and communities up and down District 5. As always, please reach out if you have any questions or thoughts on bills happening in Salem. Dick |

If you live in Coos Bay, and even if you don’t, there’s a chance you have heard of Ron Kutch. He has been a resident of the area for over forty years and deeply loves the area. “It’s home,” is a phrase that was mentioned more than once in the time spent with Ron for this interview.
Ron has lived in Coos Bay since 1985, when he was moving into the area the big industries such as timber and the port were on the way out. In the 1980’s the timber industry left the area taking thousands of jobs with it- most of which never came back. The Port of Coos Bay was seeing around 350 ships through the port yearly. Today that number is closer to 50. Another issue that faced the area was the reduction in the harvest level of federal and state timber. From 1993 to 2017, in Coos and Douglas Counties, there was a 73 percent drop in the harvest of timber.
Ron has seen all the issues that have plagued the Bay Area over the last forty years. While many left the area Ron and his family didn’t- because it is home. Ron and his wife were foster parents for twenty years, and once the children left the house, he became more involved in other aspects of the community. He currently is the Chair of the Legislative Action Committee for the Bay Area Chamber of Commerce and has served on just about every board of directors in the area.
Two of the big issues that face Coos Bay are housing and industry. The industries can’t come in unless people have somewhere to live. The Pacific Intermodal Port, or PCIP might be the solution to part of this issue. The 2.3-billion-dollar project hopes to bring in an estimated 6,000 jobs. The jobs that this project will bring in will be good paying jobs for residents and a boost to the local economy. However, there is another hurdle that Ron believes is important to address as well, “You can bring the industries in, but people still need a place to live- Housing is essential.”
Ron believes that one of the ways to get anything done is to work together. He is an active participant in weekly state Chamber of Commerce calls and bi-weekly Coos Bay Chamber calls that meets with the Representatives and Senators in the District. He networks at the Bay Area Chamber meetings and sends out information to their 500 members. He encourages everyone to follow along in the legislative process by picking a bill and following it through session.
I’ll leave you with this quote from Ron to show you how passionate he is about the place he calls home, “I moved around a lot growing up. At 26, I was ready to put down roots in a small town. I would not have picked Coos Bay, but this is the place God had for us. Over the past 40 years, it has become home. I deeply love the area. Of course, there is the natural beauty and the small-town feel, but what I really love is the _spirit_ of the folks who are trying to rebuild the community. Some are relative newcomers, some whose family has been here for 100 years or more. We were dealt a great hand years ago, but then someone came along and stacked the deck against us. Some of us are working our tails off to right that wrong. We are trying to regain the prosperity brought about by hard-working people. It will not be the same. Big Timber is gone, and it will not be coming back – at least not like it was. But we have such opportunity here – especially with the Port. We have all the pieces in place to “Git ‘R Done”. We just need a big push AND the help of our State and Federal representatives to get over the hump.”
If you are in the area, be sure to say hello to Ron and sit down with him so he can share his story of what he loves about his home with you as well.
You can learn more about the Pacific Coast Intermodal Port (PCIP) [Here](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.nrtoday.com%2Fbusiness%2Fa-look-into-the-oregon-international-port-of-coos-bay%2Farticle_472961ec-fa32-11ef-92a2-8b7e239aa2d2.html/1/0101019595fde94a-b0b66c29-f7cb-4bfd-a00e-b56f04c477e7-000000/WbSlSBEX_3v-AlV5RtpKMcb4GxfCvgTYIQefviuNn2c=396)

Each year in Oregon there are over 7,000 wildlife-vehicle collisions reported, although the actual number of these collisions is likely much higher, as half or two-thirds of large mammal collisions go unreported. It’s time to make changes to protect our wildlife and for the safety of our public. Her opponent is anti-choice extremist Brad Schimel, who, as Wisconsin's attorney general, didn't just sue to implement abortion restrictions — his top aide helped design the strategy to dismantle reproductive rights nationwide. Schimel has been vocal about wanting to implement Wisconsin's draconian abortion ban, and he has spent his entire career making it harder for people to access the care they need. body:

#

Peter,

The Trump administration wants to dismantle the Department of Education, a key federal agency that ensures tens of millions of students receive a high-quality education and critical resources. They announced this week that approximately 50 percent of the department’s workforce will be fired.

Dismantling the Department of Education would have devastating effects for tens of millions of students and their families, teachers, administrators, and paraprofessionals.

As a Navajo, I know a little something about how that goes, and after the last few weeks, I was touched when I heard that Mark Kelly was taking time out of his busy schedule to visit Ukraine. That's where unelected bureaucrat Elon Musk comes into the picture. Somehow, the billionaire found time to call Mark a traitor in his busy schedule of firing hard-working Americans, cutting aid for our most vulnerable neighbors, threatening to slash social security, endangering our national security, and neglecting the plummeting stock price of his company. Mark Kelly was in Ukraine because he believes in freedom and standing up to bullies. We're all stronger together if we defend our values - especially in the face of wealthy and vindictive bullies. ## Boy Saves Friend with Heimlich Maneuver
Nine-year-old Jayceon Branch is being hailed as a hero [after saving his 7-year-old friend](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx8kLFurDAQRb_G7ozsYcBs4eI1dPvalMjgMZ7EwMoQ0P59RD4g9ZXuOTofz-HpOfM6__cLuTjH4YjbABoapWtlcAie83tAGVwkAqolOWPRPDptWyuTg2jtCIgAWDfRoB1DAzY2I47QktGS3f2ma4PmAZ1pqogAxj8wTFNsx64TqCnwsZXqc-P1SBTzezupVNO2yOzScbx2Uf8T0Avor-uqruLzPQroV7p2AX3eJp8F9MVn4jmpLw5q9yftKhamNahEvGSeklr8-k0nFbX4MiV1qwnoZXHhdXHOvLdWoJ4Xz78IefzV5HTwEwAA__-7V2UZ), Donye Moore, from choking at Raleigh Oak Charter School in North Carolina last week. The boys were playing basketball during recess when Donye began choking on a granola bar. Acting quickly, Jayceon performed the Heimlich maneuver—a skill he says he learned by watching a YouTube video. Watch the [school surveillance footage](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx8j7FuwyAQQL8Gtljc-QxmYOjiLV07WhQOmwqHyEFB-fsq_YDO7-lJ7-u6Xn0u-bZ9-oNd2tLaUl1R4XRR4wVojT6X10oyusSMPEp2YAjsrIw2cneWNPiApEariMBaa7SZAwcNrBG9zO5dUyMQWJxhGhIhgrcUQ0j6e54FKY651XP4qfnWdk7lVZ98DqEesri9tftDjB8CF4FL733opy9vKHBBsAqRJoGLPF2891xKfmgjSG2Hz3-abP99PR3-BgAA__9S0E4A) that captured the incident.
## 105-Year-Old Celebrates Birthday with a Rave
Hilda Jackson, a spirited 105-year-old from England, [marked her birthday with a rave](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx80D1uxCAQQOHT2B0WYPBPQZHG3aZNaY1hsGfDwgojI98-Sg6QCzw9fV-P9QEUKO6f8ELjd78Wn1bJpWa8Z0KtDijcq2qd8YgS-xaNGJWYJz4OY3sYO2oLm-z5qOdJAejBb6A2mK1GxWfVkvmt8V4oMctJ6M4rKQXMylnrh22aGsXRUUm5eyaK5UAf7nRh7mx6tcEcpbzPpv9o5NLIpdba7Sm5iPWMWGrK313KeyOXN-Rys5Auijs7MVLKzGLALUPBkwmuy8E2yuVwcLNK5WDA3JNBdAxYhgsbubTZuHelEOgcxkbx_QUU_kbKfziXkT8BAAD___Hcaos) at her nursing home—trading her walker for glowsticks and dancing to a DJ. The party, organized by staff, featured an open bar, a special rap performance, and more than 250 birthday cards, including one from King Charles. [Watch a video here](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx8z71u6yAYxvGrgS0WvC8GPDAc6ShbunRoO1mEj0CEQ2QTW-7VV-4FdH0e6Sf9Py7jxeaSH7c3OwUTb3FssY7AoD8xPHExepvLPgrqTQwBAtJguBJ80ExJRZPppY4ChXVO94NE1FKqOCiHgIBX6Wk2h8aQCz6A5n0XBQC3g_DORXnVmggWfG517u41P1oKsex1DXPn6kSLSa09F4L_CJwJnLdt6_b6aq9rOP5jsc0lgueV4P_0nuD7c7mX_EVn459bLiUvUhHBbpPN5Zdsf2WuBn4CAAD___CWVVg). Described as a "cheeky lady" who's always on the go, Hilda offered simple but powerful advice for others: _“Just keep on—keep batting.”_
## Mischief the Cat Explores His City
Mischief, a cat from Plymouth, UK, has become an internet sensation for his habit of wandering around town entirely alone and [making surprise appearances in all sorts of places](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx8kMGunCAUQL8Gd9cIosKCxWQS2y5e0zTNe0uDclH6ECaAY-zXN9MP6P7k5OR8vE1v2nkX1u96R2VXOxUbJ9awDpoWKJ-Mdv6aeGWURWTYVqjowKkUzdAP1aasFIPGRppWoJACh5mj7LjpsRu6WdLKqZetaSmnkgna1ZYzRrXkZllsPwtBeIPGlZjq39GFsqH1V3xiqpe4V15tpTwyaW-EjYSN53nW-Qjhyp_XnxdB2Dj7uBI2tkJKwsa7LvAlYoZ3l7SHMSb4cN7AzTwxlCNhhjHFHb7Ggh7uGy6f8C1k-BXhXT8Qfh4hwy0Y-HHMcE_69LlKyjxO573L_UB4s-7a-X955X_Lnor9DQAA__8jhHAU). Friend, this is Gay Valimont, FL-1 candidate. I only have 18 days until my campaign is over, but I need your help.
If you look at the picture below, you’ll notice something: I’m not in focus.
[https://d15k2d11r6t6rl.cloudfront.net/public/users/Integrators/04eaa6b2-88f4-43b4-b978-7bb0708f5838/394F6E7467315A6A3657465039782F5554726333567774592F6A49706F51474E436668715A6C5265642F6553754A764161395A4D6C7641536D35496F4A384736/editor_images/Screenshot%202025-03-13%20at%2012.35.01%E2%80%AFPM.png]
That’s because this campaign isn’t about me. It’s about YOU.
It’s about the families in FL-1 who deserve better-paying jobs, affordable healthcare, and the freedom to make their own choices. It’s about the veterans who served our country and deserve dignity, not political lip service. It’s about the students who need well-funded schools and teachers who can afford to stay in the profession.
The Republican establishment wants to make this race about fear, division, and distractions —but I’m here to talk about the issues that actually impact your life. I’m not in this for personal power or political games. I’m in this because Northwest Florida deserves real leadership that listens, that cares, and that delivers.
But I can’t do this alone.
This movement belongs to all of us, and I need your help to fight back against the special interests trying to buy this seat. Chip in $5, $10, or what you can today, and together, we’ll make sure that the people—not the politicians—stay in focus. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/gay2025klemail]

| | Dear Fellow American,

Among the many passages of breathtaking beauty in _Paradise Lost_ is Milton's description of Adam seeing Eve for the first time after the Fall. They had separated for the day to complete their happy labors in the Garden, where Satan found and deceived Eve. Adam, blissfully unaware, had prepared a garland of roses to present to his bride upon their reunification.

When she appeared, he immediately knew disaster had struck: _From his slack hand the garland wreathed for Eve _ _Down dropped, and all the faded roses shed_
Imagine this scene of heartbreak! Imagine the feeling of all the world coming to ruin! Yet for Adam and Eve, as for us, there is hope in redemption. Milton is a master of building a world, describing tragedy, and depicting renewal.

Join Professor Stephen Smith as he guides us through John Milton's epic poem of power, envy, sin, forgiveness, love, and hope in one of our most beautiful online courses to date. Click the link below to register.

subject: The Republican Party of today

body:
[1]Powered By People

This is a moment in which we must vigorously oppose every part of the MAGA
agenda, including their attempt to deliver more power to Trump and Musk in
the form of a short-term funding bill, known as a Continuing Resolution or
CR.

Without allowing Democrats to participate in its writing, they expect
Democrats to assist in its passage. If Democrats, especially in the
Senate, give in, then we will have lost what little leverage we have.

For those who say, “Hey Beto, what about bipartisanship?”

Please know that when I was in Congress I was one of the most bipartisan
members there. I worked across the aisle day in and day out to get
legislation passed to serve my constituents back here in El Paso, to try
to do right by and for my country.

But, we are not living in those times anymore and the Republican Party of
five or six years ago—or the Republican Party of your parents—is not the
Republican Party of today.

In fact, it's more like the Republican Party of your great grandparents if
they lived in Germany and were National Socialists and worshiped a leader
who promised to be, and was, a dictator on day one. One who talked about
immigrants poisoning the blood of the country, who made these cynical
deals with Russia to carve up territory of countries without any regard or
interest for the rule of law or what is right or the morality or the
values that their country stands for. One who destroyed the democratic
republic within which he was elected in order to rule with absolute power.

That’s the MAGA Party of today. And I see no national interest served in
working with them at all.

At Powered by People, are working every day for the future of Texas and
our country, to fight MAGA extremism and replace it with elected leaders
who believe in the U.S. Constitution and the rule of law.

Texas will have 44 electoral college votes by 2032. Soon, there will be no
path to the White House that does not run through the Lone Star state.

The steps we take today and over the coming years will allow us to
register and mobilize the necessary voters to ultimately deliver on that
potential and promise.

Can I count on you to donate today to help Powered by People organize in
Texas and build long term political power?

[ https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20250314.M-j83N&refcode=ema20250314-240029&t=1001&akid=240029%2E444211%2EpOxOZg ]Please join us in continuing this vital work by making a
contribution—whether it’s $5 or $25, every contribution adds up to make
our work possible.

Thank you for reading,

Beto

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way for us to reach you about opportunities to act. If you need to remove yourself from our email list, click here to unsubscribe: https://act.betoorourke.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=1002&akid=240029%2E444211%2EpOxOZg

| | _**Creating Jobs and Conserving Our Environment**_
---
Friends, This week has been yet another incredible week for conservative Hoosiers, with Governor Braun and our conservative leaders in the Statehouse and Washington all working hard to deliver for Hoosiers. The week began with the announcement of the Made in America Manufacturing Initiative, putting Americans first by revitalizing our manufacturing sector and bringing new jobs to Hoosiers and citizens across our nation. Later in the week, Governor Braun signed two executive orders to reduce burdensome over-regulation, expanding opportunities for Hoosiers and further strengthening our economy, while ensuring Indiana's environmental policy is based on sound science and not radical ideology. Here at the Indiana GOP HQ, we are proud to stand alongside Governor Braun and our conservative leaders as they continue to fight for policies that put Hoosiers first. From revitalizing American manufacturing to cutting government red tape, this week has been a testament to the strength of conservative leadership in our state. As always, thank you for being a part of our Indiana GOP team and please do not hesitate to reach out if I can ever be of assistance.
---
| |
---
| | Lana Keesling, Indiana GOP Chairwoman
---
|
---
|
---
| |
---
| | _**Governor Braun Joins SBA Administrator Kelly Loeffler to Announce the Made in America Manufacturing Initiative**_
---
---
**Governor Mike Braun** on Monday, Joined SBA Administrator Kelly Loeffler and Senators Todd Young and Jim Banks to announce the Made in America Manufacturing Initiative. **What he said** : “Together with the Trump Administration, we will cut burdensome regulations and make America a place where small businesses can thrive. There is no better place to make this announcement than the Hoosier state as we look forward to the blue collar boom!” \- **Governor****Braun** , via [X](http://links.email.in-gop.com/s/c/gpXfJW-CWs0aQCt6AXwf52uxiGn4D9M0Ri6VE3rWidhDAJY4NlA0MSaI4SKAQe2QOFOUoc1oMnmhC8KlHMmWqflOm-sO5jEtVDvnNvR3iPi4dscEIUa8wGk-F_az9zb2tWUsTCD_wJ4-JmMlSPKY-_i8vClhHrufvFaD16IbBC6eBgFhiRMusJtlcabADhus3Mnh6o1a8W1MbAKocK9rKGyXVSm7tu9b4FFIIKIqjn3nuvJ5NXA-HFMGyIVAuPZN4r9Y4VS30doqoNGjvNotIK-3AR2yo664oln1Pg/Iw3p47dQSGTPrj65B77VRYDEMbWxJGpU/7).
---
**_Governor Braun Signs Executive Orders Reducing Over-Regulation and Creating Opportunity While Protecting Our Environment_**
---

**Governor Mike Braun** on Tuesday, signed two Executive Orders, the first executive order makes the federal environmental standards of the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, and Safe Drinking Water Act Indiana’s standards, and ensures that the state will not adopt new more stringent standards unless necessary. name: Pat Herrity
subject: Important Campaign Update
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Friends of Pat Herrity
body:
|
---
| |
---
| | Peter,

As you know, since announcing my campaign for Lieutenant Governor in January I've been all across the state - traveling thousands of miles and meeting voters at new events every week. I'm going to have to take a brief period off the campaign trail for the next few weeks, and I wanted to take a moment to let you know why.

Sunday night after my weekly ice hockey game, I experienced shortness of breath, minor chest pain, and swelling and sought medical attention out of an abundance of caution.

Thankfully, doctors were able to identify the source as a hereditary heart condition that many in my family have fought successfully. Yesterday morning I underwent corrective surgery and I’m happy to report that the doctors expect a full recovery in the coming weeks.

While I’m saddened to be sidelined from the campaign trail for that period, I’m tremendously grateful for the doctors, nurses, and staff at INOVA Hospital that contributed to the success of the procedure, and I’m thankful for the support of Virginians across the Commonwealth.

I look forward to resuming the campaign for Lieutenant Governor in a few weeks with the same commitment and dedication I had before the surgery and to advancing commonsense, conservative policies to keep Virginia moving forward.
---
| |
---
---
|
---
**Pat Herrity**
Springfield District Supervisor, Fairfax County
Candidate for Lieutenant Governor

subject: The Fight Against Radical Transgender Ideology
body:
| | | | | | [ ](https://ctrk.klclick2.com/l/01JPB47TW9DTHMDGBY14Z61W63_0)
---
| Peter- This week, I continued to lead the fight against radical transgender ideology that is threatening the health and safety of America’s kids. This has been one of my top priorities for several years now, and I am working hard to advance legislation to protect children from these harmful and irreversible procedures. I also applauded the Trump Administration for reaching a deal to end the war in Ukraine that now puts the ball in Russia’s court and debunked the continued false narrative about President Trump’s relationship with Russia. **My campaign is gearing up for a heated primary fight that is one year away. I am running for re-election because I want to continue fighting for Texas and America in Congress. Several opponents have already announced they are running against me, and if they win this primary, my seat will almost certainly be lost to a Democrat. We cannot allow that to happen and I am committed to campaigning hard over the next year to win decisively so I can continue fighting for our conservative movement in Congress. Your support is crucial for me to win, and I would appreciate any donation you can make to my campaign:**
---
| | [ CONTRIBUTE NOW >> ](https://ctrk.klclick2.com/l/01JPB47TW9DTHMDGBY14Z61W63_1)
---
| Thanks for your continued support. Now, here's your brief.
---
| | | |
---
| **THE FIGHT AGAINST RADICAL TRANSGENDER IDEOLOGY**
---
| |
---
| **[READ ABOUT MY BILL HERE](https://ctrk.klclick2.com/l/01JPB47TW9DTHMDGBY14Z61W63_2)**
---
| I have been leading the fight in Congress against radical transgender ideology for several years, particularly focused on how this ideology threatens America’s children. I have introduced legislation that would block federal funding for hospitals that perform sex change surgeries on minors, because there are still institutions that flout basic science and morality by engaging in these harmful and irreversible procedures. We’re standing for basic medical ethics and recognizing those who have been silenced and betrayed by a system that puts ideology ahead of genuine care. Medicine should be grounded in truth and healing—not in false promises that cause lasting harm. I have introduced this legislation repeatedly and have advanced it through my Energy and Commerce Committee. With Republican majorities in the House and Senate, and with President Trump in the White House, I am confident that now is the time to advance this bill into law. The left’s ideological movement on this issue is on its heels, and it’s time to deliver the final blow with my bill.
---
|
---
| **THE LEFT CONTINUES THE "TRUMP IS A RUSSIAN PUPPET" LIE. THAT'S WHY I CONTINUE TO DEBUNK IT.**
---
| |
---
| [**WATCH MY DEBATE WITH MEHDI HASAN HERE**](https://ctrk.klclick2.com/l/01JPB47TW9DTHMDGBY14Z61W63_3)
---
| Whenever I have the opportunity to debate leftists like Mehdi Hasan, I jump at the opportunity. Not many Republicans do this, but I think it’s important. I do this because President Trump deserves defenders who are willing to go up against the left in public settings to debunk the egregious lies they tell about his character, his record, and his agenda. There is no lie more prevalent on the left than the “Trump is a Russian puppet” lie, which Hasan continues to perpetuate it. This week, I had the opportunity to debunk that lie directly. The left bases its entire lie on their belief that Donald Trump has somehow shown weakness toward Vladimir Putin. But when you look at who was the American president when Putin invaded Ukraine over the past several years, you realize how ridiculous that belief is. The only times Vladimir Putin has invaded Ukraine over the last decade came during the Obama Administration and the Biden Administration. Putin invaded Ukraine in 2014 and Obama gave the Ukrainians blankets. President Trump took office after President Obama and gave Ukraine lethal weapons—javelins and stingers—that killed Russians. Those weapons actually saved Kyiv and stopped Russia in its tracks after they invaded when President Biden signaled he would not react strongly to “just a minor incursion.” The strange part about Mehdi Hasan’s argument here is that he actually seems to agree with the current outcome President Trump has accomplished (basically putting the ball back in Putin’s court), but as a leftist, he just can’t give Trump credit for it. As with most of the left’s arguments against President Trump, they don’t hold up when confronted with the most simple facts. That’s why I continue to engage in these debates with the left - because defending President Trump’s record is necessary and actually quite easy.
---
|
---
| **REAL PROGRESS TOWARD PEACE IN UKRAINE**
---
| |
---
| [**READ HERE**](https://ctrk.klclick2.com/l/01JPB47TW9DTHMDGBY14Z61W63_4)
---
| Secretary of State Marco Rubio and National Security Advisor Mike Waltz announced this week that Ukraine has accepted a deal that will put the world on a path toward peace in Ukraine. This is a significant step forward in achieving President Trump’s campaign promise to end the war. It is a deal grounded in American strength and puts the ball in Russia’s court. It’s a strong deal for several reasons. Ending the war and ensuring Putin obliges and never takes Kyiv is indeed in America’s interest. Our strategic deterrence remains established, and we have proven that America remains the world’s guarantor of peace. President Trump isn’t abandoning Ukraine. As he has said repeatedly, you can’t end the war by abandoning Ukraine. Zelenskyy had to be brought back to reality, and President Trump did that effectively through his public posturing with Zelenskyy and his dogged commitment to negotiating a settlement to the war. The minerals deal is a great idea for both Ukraine and the United States. It represents a security guarantee by ensuring that America’s economic interests are tied to Ukrainian sovereignty. Now the ball is in Putin’s court. Putin would be a fool to continue his maximalist policy of fully conquering Ukraine and eventually moving on to other Baltic states and Moldova, as he has publicly said is his intention. President Trump maintains significant leverage over Putin, even without additional military support for Ukraine. There are still many economic screws that can be tightened on Russia, should Putin refuse a ceasefire, and President Trump has made it clear he has no qualms about tightening those screws if necessary.
This is peace through American strength at work. President Trump is making good on his campaign promise, and we all need to give him the space to close this deal.

clean_body: | Welcome to the Indiana Democratic Party's weekly newsletter, The Kernel of Truth. The State Party will provide the most important fact - a kernel of truth - from the week. = ** Reps. Mrvan, Carson Stand For Hoosiers, Vote Against Dangerous CR Republicans in the U.S. House passed their disastrous bill to cut funding for nutritional assistance, veterans’ healthcare, and more for Hoosier families. André Carson and Frank Mrvan were the only Hoosier representatives to stand up for working families and against tax breaks for billionaires. They know that we can’t open the door for cuts to Social Security and Medicare which hundreds of thousands of Hoosiers rely on every year. Indiana Republicans “Have No Plan” on Federal Medicaid Cuts In Thursday’s Senate Appropriations Committee, Republican Senator Liz Brown of Fort Wayne admitted that Statehouse Republicans are leading Hoosiers into a situation where they have “no plan” to deal with the incoming federal cuts to Medicaid. Hoosiers will be worse off because Republicans refuse to prepare for the changes their own party are making on the federal level. More Hoosiers will be forced to use the emergency room as their primary care provider, healthcare costs will rise for everyone, and health outcomes will get even worse in Indiana. Democrats are fighting to use our state budget to fully fund Indiana Medicaid, prepare for the incoming federal cuts, and make sure every family has the health coverage needed to thrive. Each week, the State Party will highlight key policy from Democrats at the Statehouse or across the state. Democrats deliver a better future for Hoosier families, and we urge you to share this information with your networks. All across the state, Hoosier Statehouse Democrats have been holding town halls in their districts, listening to residents, and bringing the Statehouse to the people. > Trump’s hand-picked Supreme Court judges gutted a key component of the Clean Water Act and stripped the EPA of its power to enforce critical protections for our waterways.
> This decision is exactly what Big Oil and polluters wanted.
> **Here’s what happened and why it matters:**
> * The Court ruled in favor of San Francisco, saying the EPA’s permit system was too vague to enforce against wastewater pollution. That means cities and industries now have more leeway to pollute rivers, lakes, and coastlines without clear consequences.
>
>
> * The Clean Water Act was created because of public outrage over toxic pollution in rivers like the Hudson. In 1972, Congress gave the EPA power to regulate wastewater and hold polluters accountable — leading to cleaner water across the country. This ruling could roll back decades of progress.
>
>
> * Polluters are celebrating, because this ruling opens the door for even more legal challenges to environmental laws — weakening climate protections at a time when we should be strengthening them.
>
>
> * This decision goes beyond major cities. It erodes protections for small towns and rural communities that rely on clean water for drinking and agriculture. The burden of pollution will hit these communities the hardest.
>

_**“Leave No One Behind.”**_ It’s the slogan I ran on, and it’s the first thing you see on welcome signs when driving into our great state. The story behind those words started when I joined the Army at 17 — I was still a minor, so my mom had to sign the paperwork for me to join. I enlisted because I wanted to follow in the footsteps of my mentors in military school. They had shown me how to be accountable for others and overcome big challenges. When fellow soldiers needed our help, it was never a question of where they’re from or what party they voted for. We were all Americans in that moment, working toward a shared goal. To me, that’s true patriotism. **True patriotism is believing that the people around you — your fellow soldiers, your neighbors, and your community — deserve support now matter what.** That’s stuck with me, even years after hanging up my uniform. Too often, politics is centered around division. But when we’re able to embrace each other — just like how I embraced what I learned in military school and in the Army — we can create a future where no one is left behind. As your Governor, I promise to fight for that future. Thanks for reading. Elevate, Wes

clean_body: “Leave No One Behind.” It’s the slogan I ran on, and it’s the first thing you see on welcome signs when driving into our great state. The story behind those words started when I joined the Army at 17 — I was still a minor, so my mom had to sign the paperwork for me to join. I enlisted because I wanted to follow in the footsteps of my mentors in military school. They had shown me how to be accountable for others and overcome big challenges. When fellow soldiers needed our help, it was never a question of where they’re from or what party they voted for. We were all Americans in that moment, working toward a shared goal. To me, that’s true patriotism. True patriotism is believing that the people around you — your fellow soldiers, your neighbors, and your community — deserve support now matter what. That’s stuck with me, even years after hanging up my uniform. Too often, politics is centered around division. But when we’re able to embrace each other — just like how I embraced what I learned in military school and in the Army — we can create a future where no one is left behind. As your Governor, I promise to fight for that future. Thanks for reading. Elevate, Wes

body:
I'm committed to doing everything within my power to protect the American people, but I can’t do it without you.
| | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/103875257/533533368/-1072566757?refcode=jtk1108-ot-all&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NDkxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjMTNkMzg0Yi0xNzAxLWYwMTEtOTBjZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=tFeknklny9bVKMZhPusX_PQeQf6HdNdNg_fBGuAFY7w=&emci=6c88a093-5c00-f011-90cd-0022482a9fb7&emdi=c13d384b-1701-f011-90cd-0022482a9fb7&ceid=21278485)

This week, House Republicans passed a bill to fund the government that is reckless and dangerous. **It gives Elon Musk and President Trump even more unconstitutional power to shut off and redirect funding as they see fit.** It cuts services for veterans, research by the National Institutes of Health, affordable housing programs for low-income individuals, disaster relief, food programs for seniors, and so much more. There was even a provision prohibiting Congress from challenging President Trump’s tariffs.
Voting NO on the Republicans' Continuing Resolution was not a hard choice for me.
Last week I took a vote that was a hard choice for me and angered some in my community. I hear you. If given the chance, I would similarly vote yes to censure Marjorie Taylor Greene and Lauren Boebert for their behavior (and many others!). We should _all_ be held to high standards, not just Democrats, and **Speaker Johnson is a coward and hypocrite for refusing to hold these kinds of behaviors to account.**
Thank you for standing with me in this fight. There's still so much work to be done.

Chrissy

In state legislative sessions, suppressive lawmakers across the country have looked to curtail the ballot initiative process, which allows citizens to directly affect policy change by voting on proposals to change state laws and state constitutions.
In recent years, progressive policies — including Medicaid expansion, minimum-wage increases, marijuana legalization and establishment of independent redistricting commissions — have proved overwhelmingly popular with voters and have been put into law via this process.

[_**Saturday, April 12th from 9am-4pm**_](https://gop.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1d82dcd2e67c4075340c26b37&id=dbaa4f91a0&e=25844e23a8) in Lincoln, Nebraska - **[Graduate Hotel: 141 N 9th St, Lincoln, NE 68508](https://gop.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1d82dcd2e67c4075340c26b37&id=c6741227af&e=25844e23a8).** NEGOP is pleased to invite the Leadership Institute to host this workshop. Ideal attendees for the Campaign and Candidate Workshop are individuals who are looking to become more politically active and candidates, campaign staff, and volunteers who are involved or want to be involved in campaigns at any level. Topics covered at this Campaign and Candidate Workshop include:
* **Intro to Leadership Institute **
* **Are You Ready to Run**
* **Campaign Strategy**
* **Campaign Plans and Structure**
* **Messaging to the Middle**
* **Increasing Name ID Before a Political Run**
* **Fundraising**

Register & learn more about this **Campaign and Candidate Workshop** by [**clicking here**.](https://gop.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1d82dcd2e67c4075340c26b37&id=60b8db2e02&e=25844e23a8) Your registration of $15 will include _breakfast, lunch, and an afternoon snack_. Info related to dietary restriction will be provided soon.
* * *
**[What is Leadership Institute?](https://gop.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1d82dcd2e67c4075340c26b37&id=ff306a0dd8&e=25844e23a8)** Through training and mentorship, the Leadership Institute helps conservatives become successful leaders – from state legislators to members of U.S. Congress, from college students to journalists and heads of organizations – is unparalleled. While many organizations exist to increase the number of leftist activists, few similar organizations exist to serve conservatives. Because conservatism tends to focus on the power of ideas, most conservative organizations are think tanks that focus on policy or legislation. But those policies won’t get enacted without conservatives in positions of leadership to drive them forward. That’s why the Leadership Institute takes conservatives – who believe in free enterprise, limited government, strong national defense, and traditional values – and turns them into powerhouse leaders who advance these principles in places where they can make an impact. If you have any questions about this [**Campaign and Candidate Workshop**](https://gop.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1d82dcd2e67c4075340c26b37&id=1734faf585&e=25844e23a8), feel free to contact us:
* **Mary Jane Truemper | Vice-Chairman |[vicechair@ne.gop](mailto:vicechair@ne.gop) **
* **Joe Hagerty | Political Director |[political@ne.gop](mailto:political@ne.gop)**

name: AOC
subject: We can't show up just for election season.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
Next week, alongside Bernie Sanders.
#
Democrats can't show up _just_ for election season.
That’s why **I’m hitting the road alongside Senator Bernie Sanders next week**. We'll make several stops, including vulnerable, GOP-held swing districts.
While Republicans try to gut Medicaid, Medicare, and Social Security to pay for tax cuts for billionaires, people across the country are standing up against these attacks on the working class.
They deserve representation that is willing to stand with them.
[That work is complicated, but it must begin now to prevent our country from becoming a slush fund for Donald Trump and Elon Musk. **The U.S. Census Bureau just released updated population estimates ahead of the 2030 Census.** Peter: Our team has been digging into the new data, which shows that states with rapid population growth from 2023-2024 are seeing the majority of that growth in metropolitan areas. **Here’s one reason why that trend is so significant for our movement: The maps in these states are already gerrymandered, and are growing _even more_ gerrymandered as people move into packed districts. The need for redistricting reform will only become more urgent as this pattern continues.**
* **Texas** : The population of Harris County, home to Houston, saw massive growth, increasing by 105,852 people, while Dallas County grew by 19,774 people. Both Houston and Dallas were among the ten fastest-growing metro areas in the country.

* **Florida** : The population of Miami-Dade County increased by 64,211 people, and Orange County, home to Orlando, grew by 32,381.

* **Arizona** : The population of Maricopa County, home to Phoenix, increased by 57,471 people.

* **Utah** : The population in Salt Lake City and Utah Counties saw a population growth of 37,605 people, making up 62% of the state’s total growth.

* **Idaho** : The population of the Boise metropolitan area made up 58% of the population growth in the state.

Barring redistricting reforms, maps drawn based on the 2030 Census data could once again unfairly disadvantage urban, suburban, and diverse communities. **This data only underscores the need for both an accurate census as well as fair maps to ensure every voice is heard.[Please make a contribution of any amount to help fight gerrymandering and ensure a truly representative democracy.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/103876168/533536353/790884352?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_CensusRR_email_20250314-NDRC-Tier1-CensusRR_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20250314-NDRC-Tier1-CensusRR_&utm_campaign=CensusRR&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImMzMjkzMjUyLTE4MDEtZjAxMS05MGNkLTAwMjI0ODJhOWZiNyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=qeBduzHKh78rLYuMP9etUCmCVb_ekKYDomP-F-1PeTs=)** | _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_

Of course, redistricting isn’t the only process that relies heavily on census data.
Census data is also used to allocate hundreds of billions of dollars in federal funding to states and municipalities — including Medicare and Medicaid, the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, Highway Planning and Construction, the Education Stabilization Fund, National School Lunch Programs, and over 300 other programs.
Communities are counting on accurate census data to make sure they get the resources they need. But Republican state attorneys general have already sued to try to stop the 2030 Census from counting all U.S. residents. These kinds of blatant attempts to undercount communities with higher populations of immigrants and undocumented people could have far-reaching consequences for people’s daily lives.
**So we’ll keep working to ensure a fair count in the next census — which would lay a foundation for fair maps and a fair distribution of resources.**
The fair maps movement protected the 2020 Census from Donald Trump in his first term, when he tried to duck the Constitutional requirement to count all residents. And we’ll be prepared no matter what comes at us this time around. **But we’ll need your help and support along the way. **

body:
Joe is stepping up to >> Protect good union jobs Lower costs so that families can afford to live with dignity

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. Friends,
Republicans have the majority. In fact, they control all three branches of government. It’s literally their job to pass a budget.
But instead of doing their jobs, they’re kicking the can down the road again by passing a continuing resolution.
Why?
Because even they know their budget is so extreme, so wildly unpopular, that they don’t have the votes to pass it.
Let’s be clear about what’s in this so-called budget that Jim Jordan and the ULTRA-MAGA crowd love so much:
* Eliminates Medicaid while handing Jordan and his Judiciary
Committee a jaw-dropping $110 BILLION for partisan witch hunts.

This is Jackson McMillan. I am the Finance Director for Josh Weil - the Dem nominee in the special election for Florida's 6th Congressional district.
As you may know Dems have a narrow pathway towards breaking the GOPs three vote majority: winning all three 2025 special elections. For this to work Josh Weil must win in FL-06.
We are carrying our weight and have thousands of volunteers, 150+ paid staff, multiple field offices, and are plastering the district with our TV ads, texts, calls, and mailers. This all costs quite a bit of money. To be specific about 200k/day.

| | First things first: thank you for everything you do to defend the freedom to vote as a dedicated supporter of Fair Fight Action. Now, I want to give you an update on the Early Vote Erosion Act. The proposed legislation in the Georgia General Assembly _would_ have made access to the ballot box even more unequal — by allowing local governments to opt out of offering early voting on Saturdays for some municipal elections. At Fair Fight Action, with your support, we raised the alarm right away. We mobilized Georgians to speak out to lawmakers. We worked alongside allies to lobby in the legislature. And after our public pressure campaign, Georgia lawmakers removed those harmful provisions from their elections-related legislation. However (and this is a *big* however), their legislation is not final, and **lawmakers could still slip even more harmful anti-voter language into a bill before the end of session on April 4.** **So for the next three weeks, it’s still all hands on deck. Now, I want to give you an update on the Early Vote Erosion Act. The proposed legislation in the Georgia General Assembly would have made access to the ballot box even more unequal — by allowing local governments to opt out of offering early voting on Saturdays for some municipal elections. At Fair Fight Action, with your support, we raised the alarm right away. We mobilized Georgians to speak out to lawmakers. We worked alongside allies to lobby in the legislature. And after our public pressure campaign, Georgia lawmakers removed those harmful provisions from their elections-related legislation. However (and this is a big however), their legislation is not final, and lawmakers could still slip even more harmful anti-voter language into a bill before the end of session on April 4. So for the next three weeks, it’s still all hands on deck. Peter Willis,

Bernie created Our Revolution nearly a decade ago as part of his life’s
mission to build enduring progressive power from the bottom up. Since
then, our grassroots army and voter mobilization machine have helped elect
more than 1,000 progressives up and down the ballot. And we’re just
getting started.

Over 50 days into Trump’s presidency, our work is more important than
ever. We’re witnessing the dismantling of our democracy — and in its
place, Trump is methodically installing an oligarchy – a government run by
billionaires for the billionaires. A system rigged in favor of the
wealthiest and most powerful men on earth at the expense of everyone else.

Our Revolution is fighting back, growing our Citizen Action Team,
organizing to help progressive candidates win, and creating a collective,
organized front to break up corporate power and fight tirelessly for
working families. And that essential work will continue long past Trump.

To help ensure Our Revolution is able to carry on Bernie’s work in the
years and decades to come, Our Revolution is launching a new partnership

Bernie has been clear from the beginning that transformative change will
require both an inside and outside strategy that takes on corporate power
everywhere — including within the Democratic Party. As he fights
tirelessly to do that in Congress, Our Revolution works on the outside,
taking to the streets, the phones, and the ballot boxes.

Together, we are methodically building the progressive power we need to
transform our country. By engaging in local races that too often get
ignored, we are creating the infrastructure of power at the level of
government closest to people’s lives. By mobilizing the grassroots to
demand better of our elected officials, we are winning fights and showing
the strength of our movement.

generational wealth for the communities and causes you care about. And by
incorporating a gift to Our Revolution in your will, you will help build a
legacy that will help build enduring progressive power in the years to
come.

If you have any questions, do not hesitate to reach out

White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt joins me on today's show! From one Press Secretary to another, Karoline and I discuss working in the White House under President Trump. Karoline is adjusting to the very demanding pace of working for President Trump as lightning fast policy and executive orders are made. Karoline and the White House stripped the White House Correspondents Association of its stranglehold over who gets access to the president after years of dominating the press pool. Karoline also opened up doors for new media outlets that were revoked by the Biden administration, allowing fair and honest journalism back in the White House. Tina Anderson of Just Thrive Health then joins me to discuss RFK Jr's meeting with big food. RFK Jr. pressured the CEO's of some of America's biggest food companies to stop using all artificial dyes in American food. Companies like Steak and Shake are ditching seed oils already for beef tallow, following RFK Jr's commitment to Make America Healthy Again.

Sen. Ted Cruz **[called out Democrat Sen. Dick Durbin for his party's unbelievable hypocrisy](https://substack.com/redirect/0e666497-22ce-4422-819f-9ec0df4ea08a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in opposing Trump DOJ nominee Aaron Reitz for his alleged disrespect for the rule of law.
[Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/0e666497-22ce-4422-819f-9ec0df4ea08a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/0e666497-22ce-4422-819f-9ec0df4ea08a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Durbin dragged Reitz's character and reputation, accusing him of harboring "venom and self righteousness," urging his colleagues not to support his nomination. "Mr. Reitz's disrespect for the finality of court orders is matched by his disrespect for the finality of a jury verdict," Durbin stated.
Cruz eagerly fired back, "It is rich listening to our Democrat colleagues profess their fidelity to the rule of law after four years of happily turning a blind eye to Joe Biden ignoring federal law, refusing to enforce immigration law, defying the law!"
Cruz reiterated Reitz's military service in the Marine Corps and vouched for his character and qualification to serve as assistant attorney general in charge of the Office of Legal Policy.
"I for one am glad that we are getting officials at the DOJ **[who will follow the damn law!!"](https://substack.com/redirect/0e666497-22ce-4422-819f-9ec0df4ea08a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Cruz exploded.

**We won't stand for anti-democracy, anti-choice extremists buying their way into power and circumventing the will of the people.**

body:
Let me tell you about one of my favorite phrases: Be Fierce. | Peter,

Let me tell you about one of my favorite phrases: **Be Fierce.**

Why do I love it? Because it perfectly describes my outlook on life.

**It means rolling up our sleeves to do the hard things and fight for what’s right.**

But being fierce doesn’t come easy. It’s earned through perseverance. It’s realized by facing challenges head on – and helping each other overcome them.

It doesn’t matter what’s standing in our way if we’re standing together, Peter.

Be fierce,

Deb

U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Ala.) took part in a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing titled “Never to Be Silent: Stemming the Tide of Antisemitism in America,” where she addressed concerns regarding the rise of antisemitic incidents, particularly on college campuses. The hearing featured testimony from multiple witnesses, including Alyza Lewin, President of the Louis D. Brandeis Center for Human Rights under Law.

During the hearing, Senator Britt recalled her visit to Israel shortly after the October 7, 2023, terrorist attacks by Hamas, describing the experience as “gut-wrenching” and “heartbreaking.” She expressed concern over antisemitic incidents that followed in the United States, specifically on university campuses. Citing specific cases, she pointed to incidents at UCLA, Yale, Cornell, and Columbia, where Jewish students reportedly faced discrimination and hostility.

U.S. Sen. Katie Britt, R-Ala., is championing bipartisan bills to make child care more affordable and wants to put some pieces of the legislation into the reconciliation package that addresses taxes and spending.

As a mom and the youngest Republican woman ever elected to the Senate, Britt said she is focused on addressing issues parents and families face, including child care accessibility.

“I feel like it is an issue that plagues America from coast to coast, and it’s one that we should tackle to show the American people that we see them, that we hear them, and we’re doing something about it,” Britt told Alabama Daily News.

She emphasized the critical role of agriculture in America’s economy and national security. | | Senator Katie Britt Participates in Senate Judiciary Committee Hearing on Antisemitism U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Ala.) took part in a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing titled “Never to Be Silent: Stemming the Tide of Antisemitism in America,” where she addressed concerns regarding the rise of antisemitic incidents, particularly on college campuses. The hearing featured testimony from multiple witnesses, including Alyza Lewin, President of the Louis D. Brandeis Center for Human Rights under Law. During the hearing, Senator Britt recalled her visit to Israel shortly after the October 7, 2023, terrorist attacks by Hamas, describing the experience as “gut-wrenching” and “heartbreaking.” She expressed concern over antisemitic incidents that followed in the United States, specifically on university campuses. Citing specific cases, she pointed to incidents at UCLA, Yale, Cornell, and Columbia, where Jewish students reportedly faced discrimination and hostility. | | Britt pushes child care legislation, wants some provisions in reconciliation package U.S. Sen. Katie Britt, R-Ala., is championing bipartisan bills to make child care more affordable and wants to put some pieces of the legislation into the reconciliation package that addresses taxes and spending. As a mom and the youngest Republican woman ever elected to the Senate, Britt said she is focused on addressing issues parents and families face, including child care accessibility. “I feel like it is an issue that plagues America from coast to coast, and it’s one that we should tackle to show the American people that we see them, that we hear them, and we’re doing something about it,” Britt told Alabama Daily News. | | | | | | | | | Gulf of America Hat Celebrate conservative leadership and show your patriotism with this unique, high quality, Made-in-America hat. | | Follow Katie On Social Media: | | | ---|---|--- SIGN UP FOR SMS ALERTS: TEXT "KATIE" TO 27488 By texting KATIE, you consent to join a recurring SMS/MMS text messaging program that will provide alerts, donation requests, updates, and other important information. body:
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2259%2E135344%2EIalKva)

Friends --
I am writing to let you know that I just voted NO on the "continuing resolution" in the U.S. Senate.
Last night, I explained my thought process to 25,000 Michiganders on my first tele townhall, so I wanted to share with you, too.
Over the past few days, you've probably heard a lot of news and conversation about this "CR" so I wanted to take a moment to talk about what that means, and why I voted against it.
First, what is a CR?
A CR is short for continuing resolution.
Congress regularly passes bills that fund every part of the federal government. That agreement was set to expire tonight. But because Congress doesn't regularly approve annual budgets, we find ourselves in this pattern of approving short-term budgets continuously.
A CR continues funding for the government on a short term basis. If it doesn't pass, there's a government shutdown.
As a former government employee, I see government shut downs as an absolute last resort. But like everything else in government - things are different with Trump and Elon Musk in charge.
Not only would this CR result in major cuts to the Veterans Administration and some of our major infrastructure programs in Michigan, while harming our Great Lakes -- but my Republican colleagues offered me no assurances that approved money in the CR wouldn't just be redirected at the whims of Elon Musk.
And unless and until I can get some guarantees that money will be spent as it was appropriated by Congress, I can't get to yes.
That’s why I voted no, and I wanted you to hear why directly from me.
Thank you,
Elissa
* * *

👋🏻 **Wait, before you click away!** 🇺🇸
United States Senators often keep on fundraising after their election ends, but Elissa doesn't want to keep bombarding your inbox with fundraising requests.
What we will do is send you good, timely content - like this message. Stuff you might open without dread.

subject: If Republicans won’t show up to town halls, Democrats will.
body:
Here’s what’s happening:
---
**_Democrats to Hold “People’s Town Halls” in GOP-Held Target Districts Where Republicans Are Hiding From Their Voters & Constituents_** Derek, Earlier this month, House Republicans’ leadership told their members to avoid hosting town halls with their constituents. That’s because Republican members of Congress know they sold out their voters by backing Donald Trump and Elon Musk’s agenda — and they’re terrified to be in the same room as the people who sent them to Washington. **So Democrats are showing up instead.** During this congressional recess, Democrats are launching “People’s Town Halls,” a series of in-person public events in all 50 states across the country featuring local and national Democratic leaders. This is a chance for people to make their voices heard — regardless of where they live or who they voted for last year. Upcoming People’s Town Halls include:
* Arizona’s 6th Congressional District, represented by Republican Rep. Juan Ciscomani
* Colorado’s 8th Congressional District, represented by Republican Rep. Gabe Evans
* Florida’s 13th Congressional District, represented by Republican Rep. Anna Paulina Luna
* Iowa’s 3rd Congressional District, represented by Republican Rep. Zach Nunn
* Michigan’s 10th Congressional District, represented by Republican Rep. John James
* Missouri’s 2nd Congressional District, represented by Republican Rep. Ann Wagner
* Nebraska’s 2nd Congressional District, represented by Republican Rep. Don Bacon
* Pennsylvania’s 7th Congressional District, represented by Republican Rep. Ryan Mackenzie
* Pennsylvania’s 8th Congressional District, represented by Republican Rep. Rob Bresnahan

If you live in one of these districts, stay tuned for more information about how to make your voice heard at an upcoming town hall. Americans deserve to have their voices heard — even if Republicans ignore them. Peter, The Senate just voted to move forward Republicans’ continuing resolution that will rip away funding from essential programs millions of Americans rely on — _all to give tax breaks to billionaires_. The bill does not include any protections for Medicare, Medicaid or Social Security. This week, House Democrats came together to **oppose** Republicans’ CR. And today, House Democratic Leadership stood united to urge the Senate to vote no against Donald Trump and Elon Musk’s bill. But, despite our best efforts, the Senate still voted to advance the CR. It’s a disgrace, and I’ve made my feelings on this known very publicly. **The American people elected us to fight for them** — not to bow down to far-right extremists and authoritarians. The passage of Republicans’ continuing resolution will only further enable their assault on our government and the American people. Especially in moments like this one, I promise to never stop fighting for you, Peter.
