"**Texas measles outbreak grows to 259 cases, hits 2 new counties** ," Houston Chronicle's **Evan MacDonald** -- "The [measles outbreak](https://substack.com/redirect/b8b7642e-a29f-4091-9bfe-5e48be9532bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that began in the South Plains region of Texas grew to 259 cases and spread to two more counties on Friday, health officials said.

The latest update from the Texas Department of State Health Services includes 36 new cases since the agency's last update on Tuesday. Infections have mostly been seen in children who have not received the vaccine that protects against measles, mumps and rubella.

Thirty-four people have been hospitalized amid the outbreak and one school-aged child has died from measles, the DSHS said. One death has also been reported in New Mexico, which reported 35 measles cases as of Friday morning.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/532f608e-3f01-414d-a8e3-e7e64a16e55b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Two Texas counties reported their first cases amid the outbreak, bringing the total number of affected counties to 11. Cochran County, in northwest Texas, reported six cases on Friday. Lamar County, located northeast of Dallas along the border with Oklahoma, reported four cases.

Health officials have been working to control the outbreak by setting up clinics to offer the MMR vaccine. One dose is 93% effective at preventing an infection, and two doses are 97% effective, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/532f608e-3f01-414d-a8e3-e7e64a16e55b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Measles is highly contagious, so the virus can spread quickly through communities unless at least 95% of the population is vaccinated, Dr. Ben Bradley, a pathologist and assistant professor at the University of Utah, said Thursday during a virtual media briefing hosted by the College of American Pathologists.

"This is such a transmissible virus that even in passing, folks who are not vaccinated against this could be at risk for developing this kind of infection," Bradley said.

Gaines County remains the epicenter of the outbreak, adding 18 new cases on Friday. The small county along the New Mexico border has now reported 174 cases in total, about two-thirds of all cases in the outbreak.

Nearby Terry County reported four new cases, bringing its total to 36.

Dallam, Dawson, Lubbock and Yoakum counties each reported one new case. Dallam County has now seen six cases, Dawson has seen 11, Lubbock has seen four and Yoakum has seen 11.

No new infections were reported in Martin County, which has seen three cases, or in Ector or Lynn counties, which have each seen two.

Of the 259 cases, 86 have been in children younger than 5 years old and 115 have been in children and teens between 5 and 17.

Only two cases have been seen in people that have received two or more doses of the MMR vaccine; the other 257 have been in people who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown.

Prior DSHS updates said five cases had been in vaccinated individuals. The agency said in Friday's update that it learned two cases were in individuals who got the MMR vaccine after they had been exposed to the virus.

The third case was a Lubbock County resident who was believed to have measles, but actually had a reaction to the vaccine, the DSHS said. That suspected case has been removed from the case count, the agency said.

The vaccine can cause side effects such as fever or a mild rash, but those reactions are typically mild and resolve in a few days, according to the CDC." TOP NEWS "Texas measles outbreak grows to 259 cases, hits 2 new counties ," Houston Chronicle's Evan MacDonald -- "The that began in the South Plains region of Texas grew to 259 cases and spread to two more counties on Friday, health officials said. The latest update from the Texas Department of State Health Services includes 36 new cases since the agency's last update on Tuesday. Infections have mostly been seen in children who have not received the vaccine that protects against measles, mumps and rubella. Thirty-four people have been hospitalized amid the outbreak and one school-aged child has died from measles, the DSHS said. One death has also been reported in New Mexico, which reported 35 measles cases as of Friday morning. Two Texas counties reported their first cases amid the outbreak, bringing the total number of affected counties to 11. Cochran County, in northwest Texas, reported six cases on Friday. Lamar County, located northeast of Dallas along the border with Oklahoma, reported four cases. Health officials have been working to control the outbreak by setting up clinics to offer the MMR vaccine. One dose is 93% effective at preventing an infection, and two doses are 97% effective, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Measles is highly contagious, so the virus can spread quickly through communities unless at least 95% of the population is vaccinated, Dr. Ben Bradley, a pathologist and assistant professor at the University of Utah, said Thursday during a virtual media briefing hosted by the College of American Pathologists. "This is such a transmissible virus that even in passing, folks who are not vaccinated against this could be at risk for developing this kind of infection," Bradley said. Gaines County remains the epicenter of the outbreak, adding 18 new cases on Friday. The small county along the New Mexico border has now reported 174 cases in total, about two-thirds of all cases in the outbreak. Nearby Terry County reported four new cases, bringing its total to 36. Dallam, Dawson, Lubbock and Yoakum counties each reported one new case. Dallam County has now seen six cases, Dawson has seen 11, Lubbock has seen four and Yoakum has seen 11. No new infections were reported in Martin County, which has seen three cases, or in Ector or Lynn counties, which have each seen two. Of the 259 cases, 86 have been in children younger than 5 years old and 115 have been in children and teens between 5 and 17. Only two cases have been seen in people that have received two or more doses of the MMR vaccine; the other 257 have been in people who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown. Prior DSHS updates said five cases had been in vaccinated individuals. The agency said in Friday's update that it learned two cases were in individuals who got the MMR vaccine after they had been exposed to the virus. The third case was a Lubbock County resident who was believed to have measles, but actually had a reaction to the vaccine, the DSHS said. That suspected case has been removed from the case count, the agency said. The vaccine can cause side effects such as fever or a mild rash, but those reactions are typically mild and resolve in a few days, according to the CDC." * **TOP NEWS**

"**Texas measles outbreak grows to 259 cases, hits 2 new counties** ," Houston Chronicle's **Evan MacDonald** -- "The [measles outbreak](https://substack.com/redirect/4a9664b2-9c87-4716-a297-7f5e7a788133?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that began in the South Plains region of Texas grew to 259 cases and spread to two more counties on Friday, health officials said.

The latest update from the Texas Department of State Health Services includes 36 new cases since the agency's last update on Tuesday. Infections have mostly been seen in children who have not received the vaccine that protects against measles, mumps and rubella.

Thirty-four people have been hospitalized amid the outbreak and one school-aged child has died from measles, the DSHS said. One death has also been reported in New Mexico, which reported 35 measles cases as of Friday morning.

Two Texas counties reported their first cases amid the outbreak, bringing the total number of affected counties to 11. Cochran County, in northwest Texas, reported six cases on Friday. Lamar County, located northeast of Dallas along the border with Oklahoma, reported four cases.

Health officials have been working to control the outbreak by setting up clinics to offer the MMR vaccine. One dose is 93% effective at preventing an infection, and two doses are 97% effective, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Measles is highly contagious, so the virus can spread quickly through communities unless at least 95% of the population is vaccinated, Dr. Ben Bradley, a pathologist and assistant professor at the University of Utah, said Thursday during a virtual media briefing hosted by the College of American Pathologists.

"This is such a transmissible virus that even in passing, folks who are not vaccinated against this could be at risk for developing this kind of infection," Bradley said.

Gaines County remains the epicenter of the outbreak, adding 18 new cases on Friday. The small county along the New Mexico border has now reported 174 cases in total, about two-thirds of all cases in the outbreak.

Nearby Terry County reported four new cases, bringing its total to 36.

Dallam, Dawson, Lubbock and Yoakum counties each reported one new case. Dallam County has now seen six cases, Dawson has seen 11, Lubbock has seen four and Yoakum has seen 11.

No new infections were reported in Martin County, which has seen three cases, or in Ector or Lynn counties, which have each seen two.

Of the 259 cases, 86 have been in children younger than 5 years old and 115 have been in children and teens between 5 and 17.

Only two cases have been seen in people that have received two or more doses of the MMR vaccine; the other 257 have been in people who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown.

Prior DSHS updates said five cases had been in vaccinated individuals. The agency said in Friday's update that it learned two cases were in individuals who got the MMR vaccine after they had been exposed to the virus.

The third case was a Lubbock County resident who was believed to have measles, but actually had a reaction to the vaccine, the DSHS said. That suspected case has been removed from the case count, the agency said.

The vaccine can cause side effects such as fever or a mild rash, but those reactions are typically mild and resolve in a few days, according to the CDC." The small county along the New Mexico border has now reported 174 cases in total, about two-thirds of all cases in the outbreak. Nearby Terry County reported four new cases, bringing its total to 36. Dallam, Dawson, Lubbock and Yoakum counties each reported one new case. Dallam County has now seen six cases, Dawson has seen 11, Lubbock has seen four and Yoakum has seen 11. No new infections were reported in Martin County, which has seen three cases, or in Ector or Lynn counties, which have each seen two. Of the 259 cases, 86 have been in children younger than 5 years old and 115 have been in children and teens between 5 and 17. Only two cases have been seen in people that have received two or more doses of the MMR vaccine; the other 257 have been in people who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown. Prior DSHS updates said five cases had been in vaccinated individuals. The agency said in Friday's update that it learned two cases were in individuals who got the MMR vaccine after they had been exposed to the virus. The third case was a Lubbock County resident who was believed to have measles, but actually had a reaction to the vaccine, the DSHS said. That suspected case has been removed from the case count, the agency said. The vaccine can cause side effects such as fever or a mild rash, but those reactions are typically mild and resolve in a few days, according to the CDC." * Videos praising Osama bin Laden are going viral.
* Nearly 1 in 5 young Americans now view him positively.
* Only 26 states even bother to teach about 9/11 in schools.

This is no accident. This is an orchestrated effort to erase the most devastating attack on American soil from our national memory—because if they can rewrite history, they can reshape the future. We cannot let them win. With the 25th anniversary of 9/11 approaching in 2026, time is running out to stop this deliberate, radical attack on our history. That’s why we launched the 9/11 Legacy Foundation—to fight back, to tell the truth, and to ensure future generations know what really happened on that fateful day. **[**Your urgent contribution of $35 or more ensures that "We Remember" is more than just words.**](https://email.email.america1stwarroom.com/c/eJw8zrGOnDAQxvGnMZ2RZ4wNLlwkWXFFTqnSXJrIaw-HE4w5A4v27U-sTtvO_KTv79IyxeFuWfudIY4xrAyRyW8M8ePtSGX_l36-cKK28A_9K6nziz--6A2fePYOLnnM3cv4uh7K_X79__bnBk--3Rd64q_RmpKL03ltL1WwcgiiqchC24AxWoGuRqul8IPrgkTTSq-MD667Np3pjHcdeFFFiwKVkNCgVApkHYJuCJTXymgJJFgjHju1S1Sid7Buhysl51T7nKrJjtu2rI-wnmG_kt8L1W6mkLdTMOwNB-ATvTt_50Pe5-C2mGeGPYXENwycEhdwZbJf8148_fU5EJOXcOUGgFMScOVCqKrYsBxxmuKqW9aI90fXWXGz-BkAAP__8Cd2Lg)** Patriot, the 25th anniversary will be the last major milestone where survivors, first responders, and families can share their stories firsthand. If we don’t act now, these voices will be lost—and our enemies will fill the void with lies. **That’s exactly what they want.** Our national organizing committee includes former White House Chief of Staff Andrew H. Card Jr., former Defense Secretary Leon E. Panetta, Ground Zero survivor Dr. Chris Meek, and Pentagon survivor LTG Patricia D. Horoho—all committed to ensuring that America never forgets. But we need your help to fight back against this radical push to erase 9/11. **_We’re taking action—will you?_** **[**Your urgent donation will power a nationwide movement to defend the truth:**](https://email.email.america1stwarroom.com/c/eJw8zrGOnDAQxvGnMZ2RZ4wNLlwkWXFFTqnSXJrIaw-HE4w5A4v27U-sTtvO_KTv79IyxeFuWfudIY4xrAyRyW8M8ePtSGX_l36-cKK28A_9K6nziz--6A2fePYOLnnM3cv4uh7K_X79__bnBk--3Rd64q_RmpKL03ltL1WwcgiiqchC24AxWoGuRqul8IPrgkTTSq-MD667Np3pjHcdeFFFiwKVkNCgVApkHYJuCJTXymgJJFgjHju1S1Sid7Buhysl51T7nKrJjtu2rI-wnmG_kt8L1W6mkLdTMOwNB-ATvTt_50Pe5-C2mGeGPYXENwycEhdwZbJf8148_fU5EJOXcOUGgFMScOVCqKrYsBxxmuKqW9aI90fXWXGz-BkAAP__8Cd2Lg)**
* Expose the misinformation being spread to young Americans.
* Push for every state to mandate 9/11 education in schools.
* Launch national media campaigns to remind America who we are and what we stand for.
* Expand major 25th-anniversary commemorations at Ground Zero, the Pentagon, and the Flight 93 Memorial.
* Preserve first-hand survivor and hero accounts before they are lost forever.

Anti-American activists are counting on your silence They believe patriots like you will just sit back while they distort our history, weaken our nation, and erase 9/11 from the minds of future generations. Prove them wrong. We must fight to protect our history, defend the truth, and honor the heroes who gave everything that day. But we can’t do it without you. Time is running out. Act NOW. But that’s exactly what some people want. Will you let them win? Sincerely,

“This is such a transmissible virus that even in passing, folks who are not vaccinated against this could be at risk for developing this kind of infection,” Bradley said.

Gaines County remains the epicenter of the outbreak, adding 18 new cases on Friday. The small county along the New Mexico border has now reported 174 cases in total, about two-thirds of all cases in the outbreak.

Nearby Terry County reported four new cases, bringing its total to 36.

Dallam, Dawson, Lubbock and Yoakum counties each reported one new case. Dallam County has now seen six cases, Dawson has seen 11, Lubbock has seen four and Yoakum has seen 11.

Only two cases have been seen in people that have received two or more doses of the MMR vaccine; the other 257 have been in people who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown.

Prior DSHS updates said five cases had been in vaccinated individuals. The agency said in Friday's update that it learned two cases were in individuals who got the MMR vaccine after they had been exposed to the virus.

The third case was a Lubbock County resident who was believed to have measles, but actually had a reaction to the vaccine, the DSHS said. That suspected case has been removed from the case count, the agency said.

Become a PAID subscriber for $5/mo or $50/yr . | TOP NEWS “Texas measles outbreak grows to 259 cases, hits 2 new counties ,” Houston Chronicle's Evan MacDonald — “The that began in the South Plains region of Texas grew to 259 cases and spread to two more counties on Friday, health officials said. The latest update from the Texas Department of State Health Services includes 36 new cases since the agency’s last update on Tuesday. Infections have mostly been seen in children who have not received the vaccine that protects against measles, mumps and rubella. Thirty-four people have been hospitalized amid the outbreak and one school-aged child has died from measles, the DSHS said. One death has also been reported in New Mexico, which reported 35 measles cases as of Friday morning. » Two Texas counties reported their first cases amid the outbreak, bringing the total number of affected counties to 11. Cochran County, in northwest Texas, reported six cases on Friday. Lamar County, located northeast of Dallas along the border with Oklahoma, reported four cases. Health officials have been working to control the outbreak by setting up clinics to offer the MMR vaccine. One dose is 93% effective at preventing an infection, and two doses are 97% effective, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. » Measles is highly contagious, so the virus can spread quickly through communities unless at least 95% of the population is vaccinated, Dr. Ben Bradley, a pathologist and assistant professor at the University of Utah, said Thursday during a virtual media briefing hosted by the College of American Pathologists. “This is such a transmissible virus that even in passing, folks who are not vaccinated against this could be at risk for developing this kind of infection,” Bradley said. Gaines County remains the epicenter of the outbreak, adding 18 new cases on Friday. The small county along the New Mexico border has now reported 174 cases in total, about two-thirds of all cases in the outbreak. Nearby Terry County reported four new cases, bringing its total to 36. Dallam, Dawson, Lubbock and Yoakum counties each reported one new case. Dallam County has now seen six cases, Dawson has seen 11, Lubbock has seen four and Yoakum has seen 11. No new infections were reported in Martin County, which has seen three cases, or in Ector or Lynn counties, which have each seen two. Of the 259 cases, 86 have been in children younger than 5 years old and 115 have been in children and teens between 5 and 17. Only two cases have been seen in people that have received two or more doses of the MMR vaccine; the other 257 have been in people who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown. Prior DSHS updates said five cases had been in vaccinated individuals. The agency said in Friday's update that it learned two cases were in individuals who got the MMR vaccine after they had been exposed to the virus. The third case was a Lubbock County resident who was believed to have measles, but actually had a reaction to the vaccine, the DSHS said. That suspected case has been removed from the case count, the agency said. The vaccine can cause side effects such as fever or a mild rash, but those reactions are typically mild and resolve in a few days, according to the CDC."
